title: [Shortcut Guide] The taskbar indicators show on displays which do not have a taskbar
summary: Shortcut Guide can reuse taskbar-button automation state from another monitor when the cursor monitor has no taskbar, causing indicators to appear over empty space.

judgment.rationale: The report is deterministic and the current interop code retains static UI Automation state and a static button vector when taskbar discovery fails for the selected monitor.
evidence: The indicators appear on a secondary display only when that display has no taskbar.
GetTaskbarHwndForCursorMonitor returns null when no taskbar exists on the cursor monitor.
update returns early without clearing the static UI Automation element.
get_buttons reuses a static button vector, and update_buttons can return false before clearing it.
The managed layer displays any returned buttons without independently confirming that the monitor owns a taskbar.
judgment.recommended_action: Clear cached tasklist state before every monitor lookup and return an empty result when the selected monitor has no taskbar.

fix_assessment.rationale: No linked fix exists, and the stale static-state path directly explains the cross-monitor indicators.

proposed_fixes.title: Clear stale tasklist state when the target monitor has no taskbar
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The native tasklist enumerator keeps static automation and button state. A monitor lookup that finds no taskbar returns early, leaving the previous monitor's element and buttons available to the caller.
plan: Clear the cached UI Automation element before resolving the target monitor's taskbar.
Clear the static button vector before each enumeration attempt.
Return an empty array immediately when neither primary nor secondary taskbar belongs to the requested monitor.
Add focused native or managed coverage that switches from a monitor with a taskbar to one without a taskbar.
verification: Disable taskbars on secondary displays and invoke Shortcut Guide on each monitor.
Confirm indicators appear only on the monitor that owns a taskbar.
Re-enable multi-monitor taskbars and confirm each monitor enumerates its own buttons.

confidence.rationale: The stale static-state control flow exactly matches indicators from a previous monitor appearing where no taskbar exists.

issue_context.summary: Taskbar indicators are rendered on a monitor with no taskbar when Windows is configured to show the taskbar only on the primary display.
known_information: The report uses current main and provides exact multi-monitor reproduction steps and a screenshot.
The cursor monitor determines the Shortcut Guide overlay monitor.
Native tasklist enumeration stores automation objects and button data in static state.
A missing taskbar causes an early return without clearing all prior state.
inferences: The displayed indicators likely belong to the last successfully enumerated taskbar.
Clearing state at the monitor boundary should also prevent stale results after Explorer/taskbar restarts.
issue_context.analysis: The bug is not only a layout issue: the enumerator can return stale taskbar buttons after monitor-specific discovery fails. Fixing the cache lifetime at the native boundary gives the managed overlay a correct empty result.
initial_investigation: Inspected TasklistPositions.GetButtons and the native get_buttons, update, update_new, and update_buttons functions.
Traced the early-return paths and static state reuse across monitor changes.

actions.label: Design taskbar-state reset fix
actions.note: Approval starts fork-side design work only; no upstream write occurs automatically.

prerequisites: Show my taskbar on all displays disabled
steps: Invoke Shortcut Guide on the primary monitor and close it.
Move focus and the cursor to a display without a taskbar.
reproduce.expected_result: No taskbar indicators are shown on a display that has no taskbar.
reproduce.actual_result_reported: Indicators from the taskbar layout appear floating over empty space.

upstream_safety.detail: No public mutation was made to microsoft/PowerToys.
